title: A board-sampled preflop all-in equity matrix over the 169 classes
description: The artifact adr/0007 authorises: boards are sampled, deals are enumerated. Each cell is therefore exact conditional on the committed board set, and the only error is board variance -- which is why `stderr` sits beside every cell instead of being a footnote. `sampling` is required, not advisory: a sampled number that does not declare its seed, board count and batch count is a guess formatted like a fact. Range-level (weighted) numbers CANNOT be recomputed from this file, because the per-batch panels that produce a weighted error bar are not committed; they come from a generator run, which is why the derived tables this artifact supports are separate artifacts.

orientation.description: A pinned literal naming the order of `classes`, which is pokergto.cards.HAND_CLASSES_169: AA..22, then every suited class, then every offsuit class, each group in descending rank order. If the order ever changes, every consumer changes in the same commit -- the same rule data/schema/range_chart.schema.json applies to a 13x13 grid.

equity.description: equity[i][j] is hero class i's share of the pot all-in preflop against villain class j, over the committed board set. Dense and full: the transpose is stored rather than derived, so a consumer never performs arithmetic on a sampled number (ADR-0004).

stderr.description: Independent-batch standard error of the cell above it, in the same pot-share units. The diagonal is exactly 0.0 with exactly 0.0 dispersion -- a class against itself is a fair deal by symmetry, not an estimate.

estimator.description: Which function wrote these numbers, pinned as a literal so a rename cannot quietly leave the artifact describing a function that no longer exists.

sampler.description: How the boards were drawn and what was enumerated per board, in both languages. Written out because the whole claim of this artifact rests on that distinction.

boards_per_batch.description: The engine's own floor: a batch under 100 boards cannot support the error bar it is used to produce.

board_space_size.description: C(52,5). Stated so a reader can see what fraction of the board space this artifact is.

survival_probability.description: C(48,5) / C(52,5): the chance that a four-card hole set is disjoint from a uniform five-card board. Closed form, and the reason pair counts are checkable without trusting the sample.

expected_comparisons.description: boards x (ordered disjoint combo pairs) x survival_probability. The expected amount of comparison work the grid rests on; derived from combinatorics and the sampling block, so a reader never has to take a sample's word for its own size.

first_batch_sha256.description: sha256 over the first batch's integer wins/ties/pair-count panel. tools/gen_preflop.py --verify recomputes that batch from seed/boards_per_batch/batches and compares bytes, which is the per-push proof that the engine still produces this artifact's numbers; the full board set is re-derived on the schedule (adr/0008).

digits.description: Decimal places every stored value carries. Twelve would be decoration on a quantity whose own error bar is 0.003.

exact_cells.description: Class cells computed by exhaustive enumeration over all 2,598,960 boards, from pokergto.equity.range_equity(mode="exact") with the budget raised. Keys are "hero:villain" in the order the `classes` array uses. These are inputs to the agreement check, not restatements of this artifact's own numbers, and tools/gen_preflop.py --verify refuses an artifact whose keys and values have drifted from pokergto.preflop.EXACT_CELLS.

test.description: The executing test that re-runs the comparison, so a stored agreement cannot rot into a claim.
